claims_to_measure: The area of the dense chromatin core: the undilated top window multi-Otsu class inside the refinement's selection.
rationale: C7: size cuts both ways. Apoptotic bodies and lymphocytes are smaller than a mitosis, hyperchromatic interphase nuclei can be larger (Lin 2024 names immune and stromal cells as mimics).
confound: The core boundary is set by the 51 px window's own multi-Otsu, so it moves with the window's contents; it is also the stratifier of auc_area_tertiles.

claims_to_measure: Major over minor axis length of the dense core's largest piece, holes filled.
rationale: C4: a side-on metaphase plate is elongated, but spindle-cell and stromal nuclei are too (Lin 2024: stromal cells mimic metaphase); pathologists need elongation together with surface spikes.
confound: Spindle and stromal nuclei; 462 and 410 are sarcomas.
test: 5.2 outline suite: separates discs from ellipses

claims_to_measure: Convexity of the dense core's outline: filled largest piece area over its convex hull area (lower = more ragged or lobed).
rationale: C5: VCGP 2021 mitotic-like figures are "Smooth contours, circular or oval, hyperchromatic bodies (single or multiple)"; C1: VCGP 2021 "The most reliable microscopic feature to identify MF and AMF are the short spikes or blunt projections of chromosomes on the surface of aggregated nuclear material"; Meuten 2021 "short 'rods' of chromosomes protruding from the surface"; Al-Janabi 2013 "clearly visible hairy extension of nuclear material"; Veta 2015 false positives "lack ... protrusions around the edges"; VCGP QRG 2022 "MLF are smooth, MF have projecting rods/spikes"; Lashen 2021: 89 % of mitoses "retained their ragged nuclear border" on WSI while 58 % lost the hairy projections.
confound: Touching or lobulated nuclei score lower than a disc, in the mitotic direction (lobulated 0.819-0.869 vs spiked <= 0.753 on ideal masks); pixelation lowers small elongated shapes (4:1 ellipse 0.873 at r = 8). Seen on the recorded A3 pool before freezing (2026-10-09): its validity.csv row is in-sample.
test: 5.2 outline suite (spikes, lobulation, scale); end-to-end C1 deciding cell

claims_to_measure: Irregularity of the dense core's outline: convexity defects deeper than 0.25 um per um of outline.
rationale: C1: VCGP 2021 "The most reliable microscopic feature to identify MF and AMF are the short spikes or blunt projections of chromosomes on the surface of aggregated nuclear material"; Meuten 2021 "short 'rods' of chromosomes protruding from the surface"; Al-Janabi 2013 "clearly visible hairy extension of nuclear material"; Veta 2015 false positives "lack ... protrusions around the edges"; VCGP QRG 2022 "MLF are smooth, MF have projecting rods/spikes"; Lashen 2021: 89 % of mitoses "retained their ragged nuclear border" on WSI while 58 % lost the hairy projections. The outline columns measure the dense core's ragged border, which is consistent with, but not shown to be, the cue that survives on WSI.
confound: Arms paler than about 0.7x the body leave M_chr (end-to-end test: 0-0.075 at 0.7x and 0.5x), so it reads the core's ragged outline, not fine arms; touching discs score 0.04-0.10; a window-cut outline reads lower. Seen on the recorded A3 pool before freezing (2026-10-09): its validity.csv row is in-sample.
test: 5.2 outline suite (spikes, lobulation; exempt from the scale rule); end-to-end C1 deciding cell

claims_to_measure: The same concavity count on M_dark, the largest component of H > t_dark overlapping M_chr (holes filled), which keeps chromosome arms down to about 0.45x the body.
rationale: M_chr is bounded at about 0.72x the body's mean H and t_dark at about 0.44x, so arms at 0.45-0.7x body survive only here. With synthetic arms at 0.7x and 0.5x body, M_chr reads 0-0.22 and this column 0.16-0.41. C1: VCGP 2021 "The most reliable microscopic feature to identify MF and AMF are the short spikes or blunt projections of chromosomes on the surface of aggregated nuclear material"; Meuten 2021 "short 'rods' of chromosomes protruding from the surface"; Al-Janabi 2013 "clearly visible hairy extension of nuclear material"; Veta 2015 false positives "lack ... protrusions around the edges"; VCGP QRG 2022 "MLF are smooth, MF have projecting rods/spikes"; Lashen 2021: 89 % of mitoses "retained their ragged nuclear border" on WSI while 58 % lost the hairy projections.
confound: Debris clusters merge into one ragged blob (0.20-0.23), and neighbours merge at t_dark. A window-cut outline reads about 0.02 per um lower for both labels, and other rows are cut 2.5x as often, so compare it with chr_concavities_per_um only on rows where dark_touches_window is False. Added after the 2026-10-09 look at the recorded A3 pool: its in_recorded_pool validity is in-sample (uncut 0.655 against 0.635), and rows with in_recorded_pool False are its only unseen evidence.
test: end-to-end C1 deciding cell and pale-arm reporting cells

claims_to_measure: Share of the dense core's largest piece that is enclosed hole (1 - area / filled area).
rationale: C2 / C4: a vesicular nucleus whose M_chr is its rim scores high (0.78), but VCGP 2021 counts "A dark cluster or ring of chromosomes" (prometaphase) and a "linear or ring-shaped aggregate" (metaphase) as mitotic figures, which give the same mask.
confound: Both directions: membrane rims and ring-shaped figures.

claims_to_measure: High-harmonic outline energy of the dense core: harmonics 6-64 of the radius profile of the filled largest piece, over 128 x mean radius squared.
rationale: C1: VCGP 2021 "The most reliable microscopic feature to identify MF and AMF are the short spikes or blunt projections of chromosomes on the surface of aggregated nuclear material"; Meuten 2021 "short 'rods' of chromosomes protruding from the surface"; Al-Janabi 2013 "clearly visible hairy extension of nuclear material"; Veta 2015 false positives "lack ... protrusions around the edges"; VCGP QRG 2022 "MLF are smooth, MF have projecting rods/spikes"; Lashen 2021: 89 % of mitoses "retained their ragged nuclear border" on WSI while 58 % lost the hairy projections. It replaces the earlier spiky, which measured inverse elongation.
confound: Fails the scale rule on every shape (pixel-staircase noise falls with r^2); reads like a disc when arms are paler than about 0.7x the body; partial elongation sensitivity (4:1 ellipse above the disc); fixed-size spikes score 3x lower on a body twice the size (negative size confound on its own cue); may overlap chr_solidity (read redundancy.csv and auc_area_tertiles). Seen on the recorded A3 pool before freezing (2026-10-09): its validity.csv row is in-sample.
test: 5.2 outline suite (scale rule: predicted failure); end-to-end C1 deciding cell

claims_to_measure: Centroid distance from the dark piece under the candidate (101 px window, H > t_dark) to its nearest similar-sized dark piece within 10 um.
rationale: C4: anaphase is "Two separate aggregates, variable distances apart" (VCGP 2021); telophase "in separate clots" (Al-Janabi 2013). The pair columns carry the cue only jointly.
confound: A neighbouring dark nucleus of similar size is a partner too, so in crowded tissue most candidates have one; marginal AUC expected near 0.5.

claims_to_measure: Smaller over larger area of the candidate's dark piece and its partner.
rationale: C4: separating chromosome sets are of similar size; the cue is joint with the other pair columns.
confound: Neighbouring nuclei of similar size give the same ratio.

claims_to_measure: Acute angle between the major axes of the candidate's dark piece and its partner.
rationale: C4: separating plates seen side-on are parallel (near 0 deg); joint cue only.
confound: Side-by-side spindle nuclei in a fascicle are parallel too (462, 410 are sarcomas).

claims_to_measure: Mean acute angle between each piece's major axis and the line joining the two centroids.
rationale: C4: separating plates seen side-on score near 90 deg; the hypothesis that near 90 deg marks anaphase is stated here only, not as a direction.
confound: Side-by-side spindle nuclei in a fascicle give the same angle as separating plates.

claims_to_measure: Mean hematoxylin optical density over the dense core (the earlier core_od).
rationale: C3: VCGP 2021 "dark purple staining nuclear aggregates"; necessary but not sufficient (Veta 2015: "many other cellular components can have a similar hyperchromatic appearance").
confound: Nearly collinear with od (rank correlation 0.94 on the earlier pool); hyperchromatic imposters, pigment and crowding (Section 1's failing ROIs).

claims_to_measure: Fine chromatin texture: std of the 4-neighbour Laplacian of H over the eroded, clip-free core, over the core's mean H.
rationale: The only text behind a direction is one VCGP 2021 clause about resting nuclei (item 5.iv: "more heterochromatin with a more clumped chromatin pattern"); its pyknotic/karyorrhectic imposters are only "dark, hyperchromatic (darker) condensed nuclei", which gives no texture direction.
confound: Depends on size (a flat blurred disc through the refinement reads 1.74 / 1.51 / 1.26 / 1.23 at r = 5 / 8 / 12 / 16); a prometaphase clump has internal structure from its arms; a pixel-noise floor may rise with darkness, depending on the noise model (2.1 -> 3.6 over H 0.08-0.28 with constant noise, flat with noise proportional to sqrt(I)).

claims_to_measure: How much darker a band 1-3 um from the core is than the band inside it, over the core's mean H (floored at 0).
rationale: C2 / C6: the hypothesis that it marks an intact nuclear envelope around an internal clump (prophase-like) is stated here only. No source describes prophase as a clump inside a dark rim.
confound: Not specific: an anaphase partner plate in ring 3 (0.05) and a metaphase plate whose clear zone is bounded by darker cytoplasm (0.03) score too. Carries surround signal the floor clip removed from the score.

claims_to_measure: Share of the 0-1 um ring around the core above the ROI's t_nuc: nucleus or dense cytoplasm.
rationale: C9 lightness: a dark clump inside an interphase nucleus is surrounded by nucleoplasm above t_nuc, so it should read high; no counting criterion gives a direction.
confound: t_nuc admits cytoplasm (about 45 % of an ROI lies above it); carries the white-surround signal the clip removed from the score, so read it beside its correlation with white_frac_gray215_61.

claims_to_measure: Share of the 0-1 um ring at or below t_nuc but not glass (gray <= 215): pale tissue, cleared cytoplasm, halos.
rationale: C9: no verified source states a clear zone around mitotic figures in H&E; a clear halo is documented around apoptotic hepatocytes in rodent liver (NTP atlas), and this run's false positives include smooth dark nuclei with halos (546, 462).
confound: Lumps cleared cytoplasm and halos together; white-surround signal the clip removed from the score.

claims_to_measure: Share of the 61 px window brighter than gray 215 (glass, lumen): the earlier not_white without the sign.
rationale: The floor-clip run's white-adjacent false positives (A3 - A1: 316 -> 240); no counting criterion.
confound: Tissue architecture (lumen, alveoli, vessels) differs by ROI and domain.

claims_to_measure: Hue of the cytoplasm 1-3 um from the core: degrees(atan2(mean E, mean H)) over ring 2 and 3 minus glass, dark and clipped pixels; higher is more eosinophilic.
rationale: C9: VCGP 2021 item 4 "Eosinophilic cytoplasm can occur with denaturation of cytoplasmic proteins, loss of mRNA in degenerating, apoptotic or necrotic cells"; VCGP QRG 2022 "MF tend to have more amphophilic/basophilic cytoplasm (increased RNA), MLF tend to have more eosinophilic cytoplasm"; NTP atlas: apoptotic cells have "condensed, deeply eosinophilic cytoplasm".
confound: VCGP 2021: "color is not reliable"; a dark clump inside an interphase nucleus has nucleoplasm in its ring, so it reads basophilic (mitosis-like); the fixed rgb2hed vectors make pooled values incomparable across scanners.

claims_to_measure: Share of the 51 px window outside the selection that is brown pigment: R > G > B, R - B > 40, G - B > 15, gray < 180.
rationale: C8: Aubreville 2023 (MIDOG++): melanoma "pigment particles that contribute additional imposter structures ... although they have a different chromaticity (brown)".
confound: The G - B > 15 term was chosen on the same ROIs (123, 128, 291, 410) that show it working, and drops 42 % of 410's pigment pixels; red cells and pink stroma still fire at low rates.

claims_to_measure: Share of the 101 px window outside the candidate's own selection above t_dark: crowding of dark objects.
rationale: C10 / Section 1: the crowded, hyperchromatic failing ROIs (524, 527, 245); VCGP 2021 "A structure within a region of high mitotic activity is more likely to be a MF" points the other way, so no direction.
confound: Tissue type and cellularity; truncated at the ROI edge for 1.6 % of rows.

claims_to_measure: Colour off the hematoxylin-eosin plane: the mean OD over the core and its 2 px rim (non-saturated pixels), projected on the plane's normal, over its norm. Black pigment about 0.30, brown about 0.62.
rationale: C8: pigment imposters (Aubreville 2023); 211's top-10 false positives are black granular clumps.
confound: Its support is label-dependent (median chr_ns_share 0.76 for mitoses vs 0.44 for top-10 false positives on 7 ROIs); the fixed rgb2hed vectors shift each scanner's baseline (0.01 on Hamamatsu XR to 0.21 on Aperio), so pooled values are not comparable across scanners; on ROIs without pigment the mitoses score slightly higher.

claims_to_measure: Thin dark structure within 1 um of the core, as a share of the core's total H: fine arms, debris fragments, thin rims (a 0.5 um grey white top-hat).
rationale: C1: VCGP 2021 "The most reliable microscopic feature to identify MF and AMF are the short spikes or blunt projections of chromosomes on the surface of aggregated nuclear material"; Meuten 2021 "short 'rods' of chromosomes protruding from the surface"; Al-Janabi 2013 "clearly visible hairy extension of nuclear material"; Veta 2015 false positives "lack ... protrusions around the edges"; VCGP QRG 2022 "MLF are smooth, MF have projecting rods/spikes"; Lashen 2021: 89 % of mitoses "retained their ragged nuclear border" on WSI while 58 % lost the hairy projections. It is the only boundary column that reads beyond M_chr, and keeps 25-60 % of its signal when arms are 0.7x the body.
confound: Small bodies (karyorrhectic fragments, debris clusters 0.21-0.57) score high, as do thin continuous rims (vesicular window 0.34). On the recorded A3 pool its within-click AUC is below 0.5, but about 0.5 within od strata (seen before freezing, Section 2).
test: 5.8 b top-hat suite; end-to-end C1 deciding cell

claims_to_measure: Thin structure more than 0.5 um inside the core, as a share of the core's total H: granular internal chromatin.
rationale: Texture: the only text behind a direction is VCGP 2021 item 5.iv on resting nuclei; no direction.
confound: Depends on size (auc_area_tertiles); prometaphase clumps have internal structure.

claims_to_measure: Core area over the median area of the neighbouring t_nuc components (8-150 um^2) in the 101 px window.
rationale: C7: it should be +1 against apoptotic bodies and lymphocytes, which are smaller than their neighbours, but -1 against hyperchromatic interphase nuclei.
confound: t_nuc admits cytoplasm: in dense tissue neighbours and their cytoplasm merge into blobs above 150 um^2 and are dropped, leaving nbr_n < 3 on the crowded ROIs the column is for; the ratio compares the core's chromatin with a neighbour's nucleus plus cytoplasm.
test: 5.8 d unit test; real-data check on 245 and 462

claims_to_measure: M_chr reaches the 51 px window's edge, so its outline is cut by the window.
rationale: Section 4: an outline cut by the window is not the object's outline.

claims_to_measure: The M_dark piece reaches the 51 px window's edge.
rationale: Section 4: M_dark is cut by the window more often than M_chr (21 % of other rows vs 8 % of mitoses on the recorded pool).

claims_to_measure: Mean H over ring 1 (0-1 um from the core).
rationale: Section 5.3: ring_peak_prominence is a function of the ring means and h_chr_mean.

claims_to_measure: Mean H over ring 2 (1-2 um from the core).
rationale: Section 5.3.

claims_to_measure: Mean H over ring 3 (2-3 um from the core).
rationale: Section 5.3.

claims_to_measure: Share of the core-plus-2 px-rim pixels with every channel in [20, 235]: chr_resid_frac's support.
rationale: Section 5.8 a: read chr_resid_frac's AUC beside it.

claims_to_measure: How crisp the core's boundary is: mean H gradient on the filled largest piece's boundary over the core-to-ring-1 step (roughly the inverse edge width).
rationale: Covariate for whether boundary cues are resolvable on a scan (MIDOG 2022: 27.5 % of PHH3-only mitoses were "out of focus"); no counting criterion.

claims_to_measure: Number of neighbouring t_nuc components (8-150 um^2, not touching the window edge or the core) in the 101 px window.
rationale: Section 5.8 d.

claims_to_measure: Median area of those neighbours.
rationale: Section 5.8 d: it describes the neighbours, not the candidate.

claims_to_measure: The spec's version of chr_area_over_nbr: core area over the median area of neighbouring hem_101 > t_nuc components (8-150 um^2).
rationale: Kept by the defect rule (Section 2): on the real-data check the t_nuc components were often cytoplasm or stroma, not nuclei, and dense tissue merged into edge-touching sheets.
confound: Compares chromatin with nucleus plus cytoplasm; mostly NaN (few neighbours).
test: 5.8 d unit test (shared component logic); real-data check on 245 and 462

claims_to_measure: The spec's version of nbr_n: kept hem_101 > t_nuc components.
rationale: As spec_chr_area_over_nbr.
confound: As spec_chr_area_over_nbr.

claims_to_measure: The spec's version of nbr_nuc_area_med_um2: median area of the kept t_nuc components.
rationale: As spec_chr_area_over_nbr.
confound: As spec_chr_area_over_nbr.
